summary: Your bias was right: bearish, NWOG fill and Friday's low (24,976.50) as the DOL. The day still went red (-$296) because of how you ran it. You were 70% on the charts while playing DayZ, so you missed the first short. You chased a late one for -$500, then re-entered the planned short. When the lunch-hour rally hit the 25,509.75 stop you were down about $1.2k. Then you turned off your DLL and, in your own words, 'risked the whole acc gambled' on a 4hr gap. You won that gamble, but it's still the most dangerous thing in this journal. A won gamble trains you to do it again. Locking out until December 1st is the right call. Also, no Morning Check-in was filed today (the SYNDICATOR check-ins look broken), and there's no End of Day card yet.
trade: Short · NY-AM · XFA · Loss (-$296 day) · planned short entry 25,307.75 (30min 0.5 / NWOG), stop 25,509.75 (NYAM.H, ~202 pts), target 24,976.50 (Friday's low, ~331 pts, ~1.6R). Also a late chase short (-$500) and an oversized recovery trade with the DLL turned off.
rule: Thanksgiving week: no trading until December 1st, as you wrote yourself. When you come back, the DLL stays on and never gets switched off mid-session. Max 2 trades, and no games or second screens open until you're flat.

screenshots.feedback: The short box reads entry 25,307.75 at the 0.5 of the range, with the stop at 25,509.75 just above NYAM.H. The stop is above the protected high, so it was placed correctly, but it's ~202 pts. The target is 24,976.50, ~331 pts, roughly 1.6R. Price bottomed near 25,060, about 85 pts short of target, and then the 12 PM rally ripped through the stop to NYPM.H around 25,911. Your notes (30min tap, 1min slowing, 1/5min internal bearish SMT, 1min displacement) match a real setup. The problem was holding a 200-pt stop through lunch with no bullish SMT, after you were already up ~$400.

good: The bias was right: bearish, NWOG fill and Friday's low as the DOL, and price traded down to ~25,060 in NY AM.
The stop sat above NYAM.H (the protected high that made the displacement), not inside the range.
The target matched the pre-market plan exactly (24,976.50 = Friday's low).
You told the truth in the journal: DayZ, FOMO, tilt, DLL off, 'gambled'. That honesty is what makes this fixable.
You decided to lock out until December 1st. That's the right response to a tilt day, and you made the call yourself.
fix: You turned off the DLL and risked the whole account to make back $1.2k. That's the single rule break that can end an XFA. The DLL is not a setting you're allowed to touch during a session.
Trading with 70% focus while playing DayZ is why you missed the first entry and then chased.
The late chase short cost $500 and set up the tilt. Missing a move means waiting for the next retrace, not entering where you are.

When you were up ~$400 with no bullish SMT and lunch coming, the trade was managed on hope. Lunch hour is when NY AM targets stall. Paying yourself, or at least moving the stop, was the plan-consistent move.
That's at least 3 trades today, well over your 2-trade cap (yesterday's EOD already said 'No, I took more than 2 trades').

No Morning Check-in was filed today (SYNDICATOR posted nothing; Bibz said check-ins look broken), and there's no End of Day card yet. Post a manual check-in with your risk screenshot when the bot is down.
